newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT says US licence may be discussed in June/July.
newsitem.headline: NTT says US licence may be discussed in June/July.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp expects issues regarding its international procurement guidelines and pending U.S. licence application to be discussed by Tokyo and Washington in June or July, president Junichiro Miyazu said on Wednesday.
"We expect various issues, including the pending U.S. licence issue and the procurement guidelines, to be discussed during meetings," Miyazu told a news conference.
"We will be taking a wait-and-see stance until then," he said.
The U.S. Federal Telecommunications Commission decided in early March that it would not quickly grant NTT and Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co U.S. international phone licences.
One of the reasons cited was NTT's supposedly insufficient international purchases.
NTT's procurement pact, which sets guidelines for NTT's international purchases of equipment, expires in September and U.S. officials have been urging Japan to renew it.
U.S. officials have also called on Japan to scrap a 20 percent ceiling on foreign ownership in NTT and KDD.
